paragraphs: Friend, look at what Judah does here. Back in Genesis 37:26-27, he was the one who said to sell Joseph. Now he stands in front of the ruler of Egypt and offers himself: "Now please let your servant stay here as my lord's slave in place of the boy." (Genesis 44:33) Same brother, but a very different man.

Here's the lesson, baker. God can change a person all the way down, and a changed heart shows up when the pressure is on. Judah had the easy way out, because Joseph said the rest of them could "return to your father in peace." (Genesis 44:17) Judah stayed anyway. He had guaranteed Benjamin's safety (Genesis 44:32), and he was going to keep his word even if it cost him everything.

So what does that mean for you? Maybe you've got a past you're not proud of, like I had a few years in the back of a junk drawer. Nobody is stuck as the person they used to be. When you're given a chance to protect somebody, even when it costs you, you get to show what God has been growing in you. And stick with me, because Joseph hasn't answered yet.
